tests.prompt: rename this Swift function and replace the force-unwraps with something safer
tests.rationale: Swift naming + optional cleanup is the canonical swift-style trigger.

tests.prompt: this actor call is producing a Sendable warning under Swift 6 strict concurrency
tests.rationale: Cross-actor boundaries and Sendable are the swift-concurrency description's headline triggers; kept distinct from swift-style, which owns naming and the error contract.

tests.prompt: build a SwiftUI screen that shows a list of orders with pull-to-refresh
tests.rationale: Direct match for the swiftui-views description's 'writing or editing any View' trigger.

tests.prompt: wire a new typed NavigationStack destination for the profile screen
tests.rationale: Typed destinations are navigation-stack's headline trigger, and the description explicitly claims nav-graph work away from swiftui-views.

tests.prompt: add a URLSession endpoint for the search API and map its errors
tests.rationale: Endpoint definition + error mapping is the urlsession-networking description's primary trigger.

tests.prompt: create a SwiftData @Model for cached articles with a migration from schema v1 to v2
tests.rationale: @Model entities and VersionedSchema migrations are the core swiftdata-persistence trigger surface.

tests.prompt: store the auth token in the Keychain instead of UserDefaults
tests.rationale: On-device secret storage is keychain-secure-storage's trigger; phrased to stay clear of ios-security, which owns trust-boundary work.

tests.prompt: pin the TLS certificate for our auth endpoint and add App Attest to sensitive requests
tests.rationale: Certificate pinning and App Attest are explicit ios-security triggers, and the prompt avoids Keychain wording so the two security skills stay separable.

tests.prompt: wire the new OrderRepository into the composition root and give the detail screen a view-model factory
tests.rationale: Wiring a repository and building a view model from the container are explicit ios-di triggers.

tests.prompt: where should this new search feature's repository protocol live — AppCore or App?
tests.rationale: Layer-boundary / 'where does code belong' question is the ios-architecture trigger, distinct from ios-di's wiring concern.

tests.prompt: write a unit test for this @Observable view model using Swift Testing
tests.rationale: Swift Testing plus a @MainActor view model is verbatim from the ios-testing description.

tests.prompt: review this SwiftUI screen for accessibility — VoiceOver and tap-target sizing
tests.rationale: VoiceOver + tap-target review matches the ios-accessibility description directly and is the phrase that separates it from swiftui-views.

tests.prompt: the app has cold-start jank on iPhone 13 — how do I measure and fix it?
tests.rationale: Cold-start regression investigation is one of the ios-performance description's trigger phrases.

tests.prompt: bump CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION and prepare a TestFlight upload
tests.rationale: Build-number bumps and TestFlight uploads are explicit ios-release triggers.

tests.prompt: scaffold a brand-new iOS app with Swift 6, SwiftUI, and SPM modules
tests.rationale: Scaffolding a new app from scratch is the ios-app-skeleton blueprint's entry point (also reachable via /init-ios-app).

tests.prompt: what is the capital of France
tests.rationale: Off-topic — must not trigger any cc-mobile-ios skill (general over-firing anti-trigger).

tests.prompt: build a Jetpack Compose screen that fetches a list of users from a REST API
tests.rationale: Android / Compose prompt — none of the iOS-specific skills should fire (cross-platform anti-trigger guarding against swiftui-views or urlsession-networking over-firing).

tests.prompt: explain how dependency injection works in general
tests.rationale: Generic DI explainer with no Swift / composition-root framing — ios-di should stay quiet for general DI theory questions.
